title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Locksmith and door installation
audience: Locksmith and door installation owners who want repeat work and referrals from property managers, landlords and households they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Make a review or referral request after the client confirms the lock works, and make it easy to decline
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it
Write referral reward terms, including the payment condition, before any referral is made

instruction.heading: Ask after the lock is working
instruction.body: A lockout customer is often stressed at the time of the call, so ask for a review or referral after the client has confirmed that the lock works and the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step, such as a review or the name of one person who might need a locksmith, and make it easy to decline. Record the date and the answer. In one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought more reviews than an immediate one, which is one experiment, not a rule. A marketing association piece (AMA, January 2023) says that timing should match how long customers need to judge the service.

instruction.heading: Keep review requests within the platform rules
instruction.body: A review link or QR code is allowed. Do not write reviews for clients, invent them, or ask only satisfied clients, which is called review gating. Google bans discounts or goods in return for reviews. The ACCC says any incentive must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

instruction.heading: Offer the next service at sign-off, in writing
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose a dated next step. Examples include a rekey at the next tenancy change, an upgrade of an external door lock, or a key register for a building with several tenants. These are proposals to test: the research did not find evidence that these clients repeat this work. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm the client agrees before the schedule changes.

instruction.heading: Check in and re-contact with care
instruction.body: A check-in about ninety days after the work is a choice to test, not a benchmark. Before a known handover period, a short factual message may suit a property manager, but test whether it is welcome. Any message that promotes a service can be commercial, even when it is framed as a reminder, so check it against the Spam Act before sending. Record each opt-out and stop.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward and write the payment condition, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. State the reward in the invitation: a 2023 study in the Journal of Marketing Research found that stating the referrer's reward increased referrals across seven studies. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent. Check any cash-based reward with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points are not settled here.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the work, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A property manager uses a locksmith for a tenant's rekey after a lockout. She says she will recommend him to a colleague at another agency that manages several rentals in the same area. He wants to offer a credit on his next job if the colleague books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the colleague books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes the terms before any referral: the credit, the condition that the colleague's agency completes a paid job, and when the credit is applied. He asks the property manager to pass on the colleague's details, and he contacts the colleague only if the colleague agrees. He sets the credit size from his own margin, not from a published figure, and he does not promise anything he has not written down. Before he accepts a referred job, he checks the licence and insurance that cover that work in the state where it is done. Victoria's locksmith licence position is unresolved in the research, so he checks it with the regulator before accepting Victorian work.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of check-in dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review while the customer is still waiting for the lock to be finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the lock works.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo or review without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or accepting a referred job the licence does not cover.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and honour it at once. Check the licence and insurance before accepting any referred job.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. Client details are personal information where the Privacy Act applies. Whether it applies to your business is not settled in the research, so check the OAIC's small business guidance.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder. Every commercial message needs a working unsubscribe, honoured within five working days.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only work your licence and insurance cover in the state where it is done. Victoria's locksmith licence position is unresolved, and New South Wales and Queensland require locksmith licences. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the lock works, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next service in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the lock is fitted, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the lock works
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A property manager wants to post a review with her name and a photo of the fitted lock. What do you need?
options: Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional
Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does this lesson say to propose the next service?

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only.

AMA, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Timing should match how long customers need to judge the service.
Google Business Profile Help, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Review links and QR codes; no discounts or goods for reviews.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on review content.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position it describes was not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Stating the reward in the invitation increased referrals. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022. Used for the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Factual service reminders can be commercial messages.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown. Consent, identification and unsubscribe honoured within five working days.
Parliament of Victoria, petition 654, https://www.parliament.vic.gov.au/get-involved/petitions/reduce-scam-locksmith-operators/, presented 5 February 2026. Victorian licence position not settled.
